metadata.title: How to make a Fabric Strap watch - DIY Wrist Watch with Fabric Strap (Hindi)
metadata.description:

transcript.text: Hey, Welcome to Peej Fashion
If you want to give your old wrist watch a new fabric strap, then keep on watching.
Things that you need
an old wrist watch, an inch tape, a needle & thread,
a tailoring chalk, scissors, cutter,
and a printed chiffon fabric.
Firstly we will remove the straps from the watch.
Seam rip with cutter and pull out the strap.
Please make sure that your wrist watch has this kind of loop, so that we can insert the fabric.
Remove the strap from the other side as well.
Measure the wrist round. In most of the cases it will be 6.5" to 7"
Now we need to cut the fabric
Mark 10 inches width (same for all wrist sizes)
and now mark length. (wrist round x 5 + 1 inch for seam)
We have the strip of fabric which is 10 inches wide and
34 inches long (33 inches + 1 inch seam allowance)
Now we will fold the fabric and stitch from the length.
You can use needle & thread or you can use sewing machine for stitching.
Turn right side out.
Now loop the fabric strip from the watch.
Fold the end inside and stitch it.
Use needle & thread or sewing machine (according to your preference)

Your Wrist Watch with Fabric Strap is
Ready.
I made one in Blue as well.
You can watch our other videos too.
Thanks for Watching

summary.brief: A woman makes a colorful fabric strap for an old wristwatch and displays the finished watch.
summary.detailed: The video opens with the Peej Fashion logo and title screens, then a woman holds an old wristwatch. She removes the original metal strap with a cutter, confirms that the watch case has a loop, and measures her wrist (about 6.5–7 inches). She marks a printed chiffon fabric to a width of 10 inches and a length equal to five times the wrist circumference plus one inch for seam allowance, cuts the strip, folds it, and stitches along the long edge using a needle and thread (or a sewing machine). After stitching, she turns the strip right‑side‑out, loops it onto the watch case, folds the ends inside and stitches them to secure the new strap. The completed watch with the fabric strap is shown on her wrist, with the fabric tail visible. The tutorial ends with promotional graphics and the “xoxo Peej” sign‑off.

action.detailed: Cut the fabric to the marked dimensions, fold and stitch it into a long strip, turn the strip right‑side‑out, loop it onto the watch case, fold the ends inside and stitch them, then wear the finished fabric‑strap watch.

summary.brief: A woman removes a watch’s metal band and replaces it with a sewn fabric strap.
summary.detailed: The tutorial starts with the presenter taking an old wrist‑watch, cutting off its original metal straps and confirming that the case has a loop for a new strap. She measures her wrist, then marks a printed chiffon fabric strip that is 10 inches wide and long enough for five times the wrist circumference plus a 1‑inch seam allowance. The strip is cut, folded lengthwise, and stitched along the long edge using needle and thread (or a sewing machine). After stitching, she turns the fabric tube right‑side‑out, threads it through the watch’s strap loop, folds the excess end inside, and stitches it to secure the new strap. summary.brief: A woman builds a fabric strap for a wristwatch by cutting, measuring, pinning and sewing the band.
summary.detailed: The clip begins with a close‑up of the woman’s left wrist wearing a watch wrapped in a bright floral fabric band. She removes the band, places the fabric strip on a white surface and secures it with a pin. A roll of string is shown, and she threads the string through a small tool before pulling it through the fabric. summary.brief: A woman removes a watch’s original band, cuts a piece of colorful fabric, and measures her wrist for a new fabric strap.
summary.detailed: The segment begins with a close‑up of a woman’s left hand wearing a silver‑cased watch whose strap is a bright, multicoloured fabric; pink nail polish and a small circular tattoo are visible on her wrist. She points to a white title card that reads “DIY FABRIC STRAP WRIST WATCH” and rotates her wrist, showing the strap and her bracelet. The scene then cuts to a white tabletop where the pink‑silver watch is placed next to a yellow measuring tape, a spool of red thread, a pink foam piece, scissors and a fabric cutter. The woman lifts a floral‑printed fabric, folds it, and holds it beside the watch. She uses the scissors to cut off the coloured portion of the existing watch strap, then switches to pliers to cut away the original metal band while still holding the watch. Finally, she wraps the yellow measuring tape around her left wrist, pulls it snugly and reads the measurement, which shows about 8.5 inches. Throughout, on‑screen graphics such as a subscribe prompt and watermarks appear, but the visual focus remains on the hands performing the cutting and measuring actions against a plain white background.

action.detailed: Using pliers, cut the original metal band of the watch, then cut a piece of the colorful fabric with scissors, and finally wrap a yellow measuring tape around the wrist to record its circumference.

summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video opens with the Peej Fashion logo and title screens, then a woman holds an old wristwatch. She removes the original metal strap with a cutter, confirms that the watch case has a loop, and measures her wrist (about 6.5–7 inches). She marks a printed chiffon fabric to a width of 10 inches and a length equal to five times the wrist circumference plus one inch for seam allowance, cuts the strip, folds it, and stitches along the long edge using a needle and thread (or a sewing machine). After stitching, she turns the strip right‑side‑out, loops it onto the watch case, folds the ends inside and stitches them to secure the new strap. The completed watch with the fabric strap is shown on her wrist, with the fabric tail visible. The tutorial ends with promotional graphics and the “xoxo Peej” sign‑off.

llm.system_prompt:
You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to either of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   A video can match neither, one, or both. Be strict — when in doubt,
   say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
